# Roadmap

Part of the [whagent-net product brief](../PRODUCT.md).

Each `Cn` below is defined in [`02-capability-map.md`](02-capability-map.md).

_`Status` is each milestone's **current** delivery status, derived from krill's append-only `milestone_status_event` history (`store.MilestoneStatusEventStore.CurrentStatuses`). A milestone with no recorded transition is `not started` — that is krill's own derivation from the absence of history, not a rendered default._

5 milestones (0 abandoned), one block each below.

### M1 — An operator can run a capped, tool-enabled session as themselves against ASS's MCP server from Claude Code, and read its transcript

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9, C11, C12
- Must not foreclose: LB1, LB2, LB3, LB4, LB5, LB6, LB7
- Deliberately deferred: headless service-account callers (C10 → M2; LB2's `kind human|service` subject shape is fixed in M1 so nothing forecloses it); live event following for programmatic clients (C17 → M2); cold-tier reads and the archiver (C18 → M2; the hot tier is not TTL'd until the archiver exists, so nothing ages out in M1 and "no retention job" is an M1 design constraint); any UI (C13–C16 → M2)
- FR budget: 12

Must not foreclose (rationale): LB1, LB2, LB3, LB4, LB5, LB6, LB7 — M1 establishes all seven. LB1 and LB7 are the two M1 does not consume itself: the transcript record must be published to the bus on commit in its final shape even though nothing reads it yet, so that C14/C17/C19 can bind to it later without a re-publish format.

Design-time notes (not FRs): Temporal workflow versioning discipline for open long-lived sessions across deploys is an M1 NFR (Q8). `iss` is a real column on both `subject` and `on_behalf_of` (LB2) — no Keycloak-only CHECK, no bare `sub` — so a non-Keycloak issuer in M3 is a row, not a migration. Consumer-side work M1 depends on, owned by `audience_score_system` under C12: mount `libs/go/whagent`'s verifying middleware ahead of `auth` on ASS's MCP server, and have ASS's `CallerResolver` map the verified `(iss, sub)` → `person_id` from day one (keyed on the pair, so the M3 Google issuer is one more row-set, not a re-key); a Keycloak role for the first agent must exist in the realm. Budget honesty: eleven capabilities in twelve FRs is one FR each plus one spare — design must write C1 (gRPC + Claude Code MCP surface) and C6 (turn cap, cost cap, estimation) tightly. If the draft still exceeds budget with every FR tracing, the next cut is already agreed: C9 stays, C8's role check stays, and C5's per-session override moves to M2 (the definition-level model choice stays).

### M2 — An operator can start a session and watch any session — live or long finished, whoever started it — from a standalone web UI

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C10, C13, C14, C15, C16, C17, C18, C27
- Must not foreclose: LB1, LB2, LB3, LB6, LB7
- Deliberately deferred: embedding in another domain's UI (C19 → M3); per-turn context view (C24 → Later); cross-session rollups (C25 → Later); parent/child session views (C21 → Later); agent definition authoring in the UI (not a mapped capability — definitions stay config-seeded per LB5 until someone asks) (→ Unscheduled (not a mapped capability; until someone asks)); Pre-agreed over-budget cut, taken only if the design draft exceeds budget with every FR tracing correctly, in this order: C17 → M3 first (C14 already gives humans live following, and M3's host UI subscribes to the exchange directly per LB7, so nothing in M3 depends on C17), then C16 → Later. Never widen an FR to keep a capability in.
- FR budget: 12

Must not foreclose (rationale): LB1, LB2, LB3, LB6, LB7 — the UI reads the LB1 record via the LB7 exchange (no private read path), and the cold tier stores that same record, so a finished session's transcript read from S3 is the record the live view showed; "started by" renders from LB2's subject columns without adding a UI-only identity notion; usage shows from LB6's per-turn rows rather than a counter; LB3 because C10 is the first time the persona JWT is minted for a service subject with no human behind it — same claim set; `sub` is the acting service subject when the caller acts for itself (LB2: `on_behalf_of` = `subject`), never a second claim shape for service sessions.

Design-time notes (not FRs): C10 is carried from M1 and is expected to be one FR — a client-credentials caller passes the same C8 role check with `on_behalf_of` = the service subject and `kind = service` — and C15's "who started it" is what makes those sessions visible. C14 and C17 are independent consumers of the same bus (Q7); the UI binds `htmxsse.Hub` to `whagent_net/events` directly, and `api.StreamEvents` fronts the same exchange for clients without RMQ credentials. C18 brings the archiver (batch → gzip → S3 → index row; `manmanv2/log-processor/archiver` is the precedent) and, with it, the first hot-tier retention rule; the read path must resolve a session's transcript across hot and cold tiers without the reader knowing which served it.

### M3 — An ASS Creator / Analyst can run a research agent inside ASS's web UI that acts as them against ASS's MCP tools

- Status: not started
- Delivers: C19, C20
- Must not foreclose: LB1, LB2, LB3, LB7
- Deliberately deferred: parent/child sessions (C21 → Later); mid-flight tool-set changes (C23 → Later); per-turn context debugging (C24 → Later); usage rollups (C25 → Later); Slack front door (C26 → Later)
- FR budget: 12

Must not foreclose (rationale): LB1, LB2, LB3, LB7 — the embedded component is a reader of the same record and exchange as the standalone UI, and the on-behalf-of chain is the same LB3 credential ASS already verifies since M1.

Prerequisites (outside this product, before M3 enters design): an amendment to ASS's brief (`/project-manager:product` on ASS's tracking issue #1562) touching three things together — its LB4, the "never a chat/reasoning surface" clause of its LB5, and its non-goal — narrowing "no hosted agent loop, ever" to "ASS does not host its *own* agent loop — it embeds whagent-net's", since C20 puts the research conversation inside ASS `web`; and ASS `web` taking a RabbitMQ dependency so it can run its own `htmxsse.Hub` on `whagent_net/events` (Q7). Open for M3 design, not decided here: ASS `web`'s sign-in is Google via `web/auth`, not Keycloak — how a signed-in ASS Person becomes an LB2 on-behalf-of subject. LB2's `iss`+`sub` shape already admits a non-Keycloak issuer (`iss = accounts.google.com`, `sub = <google sub>`, `kind = human`, no schema change), and C8's role check applies to the acting subject; whether the host decides which Persons may run its agent (with its service account holding the role) or Google is brokered through Keycloak so the Person gets a Keycloak `sub` is authorization policy — LB2 lists it under Stays cheap, and architect confirms the choice at M3 design.

### M4 — An operator running an agent against a large tool catalog gets a session whose model searches for and loads only the tool definitions it needs on a given turn, instead of the whole allowed set being present from turn 1

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C22, C29
- Must not foreclose: LB5
- Deliberately deferred: the exact interaction between a searched-in tool and the already-enforced `allowed_tools` ceiling (C22) — left to design time (→ M4 design pass); UI-driven tool selection/browsing — stays gated on C13–C16 regardless of this milestone (→ Gated on C13–C16 (M2))
- FR budget: 12

Must not foreclose (rationale): LB5 — `tool_set`/`allowed_tools` (C22) is a ceiling this milestone's search-first load path must compose with, not supersede: a searched-in tool still has to clear `allowed_tools` before it reaches `Tools`. Reserving the future meta-tool's name across every domain server's tool namespace was flagged as a candidate load-bearing decision during this amendment's reconciliation; architect ruled it is **not** load-bearing (no domain server today has a colliding name, and M4's own design pass can pick one specifically to avoid whatever exists by then) — no new `LBn` was added, and this milestone's design pass picks the reserved name itself.

Design-time notes (not FRs): `ListToolDefinitions`'/`CallModelInput.Tools`' per-turn shape becomes path-dependent on prior turns and model behavior instead of purely a function of the agent definition — new for whagent-net, worth flagging to whoever writes the FRs. A searched-in tool definition is itself a context cost `worker/context.go`'s budget accounting does not currently account for. Any `SessionWorkflow`/`processTurn` control-flow change here needs a `workflow.GetVersion` gate per NFR1, since `ActivityListToolDefinitions`'s per-turn behavior would change for already-open sessions across a worker deploy. See `whagent_net/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "Deferred/searched tool loading" open item for the fuller writeup this milestone formalizes.

### M5 — An operator or on-call viewer watching a session in whagent-net's own web UI can tell at a glance whether a turn is processing or the session is idle

- Status: shipped
- Delivers: C30
- Must not foreclose: LB7
- Deliberately deferred: real LLM-token/partial-content streaming of an in-progress turn's content — proposed and withdrawn during this amendment's own drafting, explicitly not wanted yet per the requester; would be its own future milestone/amendment, with a real LB1/LB6/LB7 discussion at that point. (→ Future milestone/amendment (unscheduled)); Embedding this indicator in a host domain's UI (C19 → M3) — M3's `embed` package does not exist yet and M3 is still blocked on its own ASS-brief prerequisite.
- FR budget: 8

Must not foreclose (rationale): LB7 — if making the badge/composer flip the instant `sessions.status` changes (rather than waiting for the next transcript-event push or the 30s heartbeat) needs its own bus signal, that signal is added within `whagent_net/events`' existing exchange/routing-key scheme, not a new package or a second bus contract.

Design-time notes (not FRs): the transcript's own live-update behavior (C13/C14) already works — `whagent_net/ui/templ_render.go`'s missing htmx SSE extension script tag, which had silently broken it client-side despite the backend publishing correctly, shipped as an out-of-band fix (PR #2737, tracked on tracking issue #2083 as amendment slug `sse-ext-script-missing`) ahead of this milestone's own design pass. M5's design pass can assume that fix is in place and build the processing/idle indicator on top of a transcript view that already updates live, rather than re-deriving or re-verifying it. Visual treatment for "processing" (spinner icon, animated badge, disabled/greyed composer while running, or some combination) is the design-time choice this milestone exists to make; `OwnerControls`/`isTerminalSessionState` (session.templ) already have a hook shape for state-conditional composer rendering that a `running`-state treatment can likely extend.
